title: Sitcoms Part II
summary: Part two of a two-part Stuff You Should Know episode on sitcoms. The hosts cover sitcom ratings dominance (I Love Lucy's 1953 rating versus Friends), the shift to videotape with All in the Family in 1971, serious "very special episodes" (All in the Family's Edith assault episode, Maude's abortion episode, Different Strokes' child exploitation two-parter, a By the Bell episode), syndication money, and groundbreaking character-driven shows like The Jeffersons, Good Times and Sanford and Son. They discuss great moments (I Love Lucy's conveyor belt episode and Little Ricky's birth, The Mary Tyler Moore Show's "Chuckles Bites the Dust," Happy Days' "jumping the shark," the MASH finale, Ellen's coming out), tropes (the center couch, breaking the fourth wall), spinoffs (All in the Family's spinoff family, Cheers to Frasier), animated sitcoms (The Flintstones, The Simpsons), the final episode of the Bob Newhart Show, and recast characters ("the other Darren" on Bewitched and other recasts). Includes ad breaks and a closing sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and sitcom ratings
segments.summary: The hosts open the second part of the sitcom episode, noting sitcoms' dominance in top ratings and comparing I Love Lucy's 1953 rating to Friends' 2001 rating.

segments.title: Videotape and the 1970s sitcom era
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the switch from film to videotape starting with All in the Family in 1971, and how sitcoms of the 1950s through 1960s competed with variety, quiz and Western shows.

segments.title: Very special episodes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss sitcoms tackling serious issues, including All in the Family's Edith assault episode, Maude's abortion two-parter, and Different Strokes' child exploitation episode, along with the hallmark of no audience applause.

segments.title: Very special episodes across shows and syndication
segments.summary: The hosts note that many shows did very special episodes, including a By the Bell episode about speed addiction, and then turn to sitcom peak years and the financial value of syndication.

segments.title: Character-driven comedy and representation
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how sitcom characters let audiences identify with or observe other lives, including working-class and wealthy families, and the 1970s Black sitcoms The Jeffersons, Good Times and Sanford and Son, plus Norman Lear's casting of Sherman Helmsley.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: A short ad break with sponsor reads.

segments.title: Great sitcom moments
segments.summary: The hosts list memorable episodes: I Love Lucy's conveyor belt and Little Ricky's birth, Mary Kaye and Johnny's preservation problem, and the Mary Tyler Moore Show's 'Chuckles Bites the Dust.'

segments.title: Jumping the shark and landmark finales
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Happy Days' 'jumping the shark' moment, the origin of the phrase, the MASH finale's record audience, and Ellen's coming out episode and the backlash from Jerry Falwell.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: A short ad break with sponsor reads.

segments.title: Sitcom tropes: couch, fourth wall, spinoffs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the center-couch set layout, breaking the fourth wall, and sitcom spinoffs including All in the Family's many spinoffs, Happy Days, Cheers to Frasier, and The Cosby Show to A Different World.

segments.title: Animated sitcoms and the Bob Newhart Show finale
segments.summary: The hosts cover The Flintstones as an early animated sitcom leading to The Simpsons and others, then praise the final episode of The Bob Newhart Show, revealed to be a dream.

segments.title: Recasting actors and the other Darren
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 'other Darren' trope from Bewitched, plus other sitcom recasts such as Seinfeld's Morty, Mitch Hurwitz's Arrested Development recasting, and Different Strokes and Bewitched recasts, then close the episode with the sign-off.
